To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a 0 d dry period (DP), without use of dry-cow antibiotics, had no effects on udder infections in the dry period and early lactation but may have negative effects on udders in later lactation, compared with a 30-d DP.

the effects of a 30 d dry period without use dry cow antibiotics on the incidence of clinical mastitis and on somatic cell count were comparable to the effects of a short dry period of 0 d, but the incidence of subclinical mastitis and somatic cell score was greater for cows fed a standard energy level after a short dry period than after a long dry period.
the udder health status of dairy cows that were not given dry cow antibiotics and that were fed a standard energy level was not affected by the length of the dry period.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a short or no DP and dietary energy level on udder heath of dairy cows.
the effect of dry period length on the incidence of clinical and subclinical mastitis in dairy cows.
the effects of a 30 d vs. a 0 d dry period on udder and metabolic health of dairy cows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of a 0 or 30 d dry period without the use of dry cow antibiotic on the udder health is not clear.
the 0 d dry period with a low energy diet is the preferred option to reduce the incidence of mastitis and to improve udder health, compared with the 0 d and 30 d dry periods.
a 0 d dry period with a low energy ration seems to be a good alternative to a 30 d dry period without the use of dry cow treatments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of DP length on udder heath were not as clear as expected, but a reduced energy level in early lactation did improve udder health.

cows with a shorter DP without the use of dry cow antibiotic treatment should be fed an energy level required for their milk yield to avoid negative effects on udder and metabolic health in early and mid lactation.
cows with a short dry period (0dDP) had higher milk production, higher energy balance and higher plasma insulin concentration than cows with a longer dry period (30 dDP).
The main takeaway from our work is that
cows that have a 0 d dry period without use antibiotics should receive a low dietary energy level to improve udder health.
cows that are not dried off with dry cow antibiotics and are fed a high energy diet after a short DP may be at risk for udder health problems later in lactation.
a 0 d dry period with use of a low energy ration seems to improve udder health.
